key_insight: The study proposes an auditable framework that combines LLM-assisted evidence extraction with deterministic checks and human oversight to produce versioned, traceable systematic review outputs.
clinical_relevance: This could improve transparency and reliability in evidence synthesis used to inform clinical and prognostic decisions, but it is not yet proven to improve patient care or generalize broadly.
method: LLM agents interpreted sources and extracted data
Deterministic code enforced statistical rules and handling of corrections
Investigators resolved material ambiguities and authorized release
evidence_signal: In one registered prognostic review, the team documented 50 root-cause events, evaluated six integrity domains, and compared two implementations across 1,217 numerical checks plus 94 byte-level file comparisons.
watch_item: This was a retrospective, single-project evaluation without an external comparator, so broader validity and real-world benefit remain unproven.
paper_title: An auditable evidence compiler for large language model-assisted systematic reviews
